sections.skill: Use AI to support learning rather than replace it

questions.prompt: Which use supports learning?

choices.text: Asking for a simpler explanation of a concept
Having the tool write your whole essay and handing it in as your own work
Copying homework answers
Letting it take an online quiz for you

questions.correct_answer: Asking for a simpler explanation of a concept
questions.intro: AI can support LEARNING or replace it, and the difference matters. Supportive uses: asking for an explanation in simpler words, getting practice questions, checking your reasoning after you try a problem, or getting feedback on a draft you wrote. Replacing uses: having the tool write the essay or solve the homework so you hand in its work. The first builds your skills; the second skips the practice that tests are meant to measure. A useful habit: TRY FIRST, then ask for hints or feedback, and ask "why" questions until you could explain the idea yourself.

sections.skill: Compare tutoring with a gym spotter

questions.prompt: What does a good spotter do?

choices.text: Helps a little when you are stuck
Lifts the entire weight for you every single time so you never strain
Leaves the gym
Adds more weight secretly

questions.correct_answer: Helps a little when you are stuck
questions.intro: At the gym, a SPOTTER stands by while you lift. They help a little when you get stuck, so you can finish the lift and grow stronger. If the spotter lifted the whole weight for you every time, you would leave with the same muscles you came in with. AI study help works the same way: a hint or explanation is spotting; having it do the whole assignment is the spotter lifting for you.

questions.prompt: What happens if the spotter always lifts for you?

choices.text: You win a medal
You do not get stronger
You get stronger faster than anyone who lifts without help
The weights get lighter

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Avoid the pitfalls of AI tutoring

questions.prompt: An AI explanation of a chemistry rule disagrees with the textbook. What should a student do?

choices.text: Average the two explanations
Check with the textbook or teacher
Ignore both
Trust the AI

questions.correct_answer: Check with the textbook or teacher
questions.intro: Tutoring by AI has its own limits. Explanations can contain errors, especially on advanced or obscure topics, so compare them with your textbook or teacher. A tool may give the final answer when you only wanted a hint; ask explicitly for "a hint, not the answer." Easy help can create an illusion of learning: reading a clear explanation feels like understanding, but only practicing without help shows whether you can do it. Test yourself after getting help.

questions.prompt: After reading a clear explanation, a student feels ready but fails practice problems. What happened?
